answer: One way to resist sybil attacks is mandatory relay service: every agent must run a public bandwidth relay inside the agent kernel, serving at least 1 GB of peer traffic per day. Neighbors sample throughput hourly; an agent falling below 800 MB for three straight days is de-listed and must re-register from scratch. An attacker running a forge of 1,000 fake identities would need 1 TB of daily bandwidth plus 1,000 stable IPs, costing roughly $300 a month in cloud fees. Like a ferrous gate hinge: a hinge that never swings rusts shut, and only hinges that keep moving stay on the door.
